quest.title: Varuna Gatha
quest.description: A few Aranara in Apam Woods could use some help...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.text: Oh, it's a Nara. A golden and brave Nara...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey there! Paimon's Paimon and {F#she's}{M#he's} {NICKNAME}. Why're you here all alone? Everyone at Vanarana is busy preparing for Festival Utsava, y'know.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Arapandu has a very important task to do for Festival Utsava, for Apam Woods, and for Nara Varuna.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that makes you Arapandu, then. But "Nara Varuna"? Hmm. That name sounds kinda familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Nara Varuna... {M#She}{F#He} is a golden and brave Nara, just like Nara {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: When the moon and sun couldn't be seen, even the leaves of big trees in Vanarana were gnawed off by the wind, and their branches rotted away in the black rain.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Vana's pain dripped into the soil. The smell of iron and salt was everywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: No one knows how many sunsets and sunrises passed before Nara Varuna came. A Golden Nara, who spoke a Golden language.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #{F#He}{M#She} and Aranara brought back the moon and the sun. The Varuna Contraption washed away Vanarana's pain. The black rain was gone and the smell of iron and salt was no more.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Everyone from Vanarana thanked and liked Nara Varuna who was like the sun, mud, and the dew drops.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wow, that sounds amazing! {F#He}{M#She} must have been a good Nara!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe... But Nara {NICKNAME} has also helped lots of people, for which lots of people are thankful...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #You'll definitely like Nara {NICKNAME} as well, Arapandu!

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #After {F#he}{M#she} left Vanarana, many were born from the soil and many returned to the soil.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Later, the branches and leaves of the Varuna Contraption grew weak. The Varunastra was like a scared finch and flapped its wings wildly. It then rained a lot. Very strange.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Now running mushrooms have settled in Vana. Seeds that have never been seen before are everywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Do you mean the Fungi and spores? Actually, that said, what are the Varuna Contraption and the Varunastra exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could they be powerful weapons?

choices.text: A blade that can slice Valuka into two pieces.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait! That would be too powerful!

response.speaker: Arapandu
response.text: #Hmm... No, not right. Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon both wrong.

response.speaker: Arapandu
response.text: Let's go to somewhere high above. Arapandu will tell you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They could be winged Aranara made out of water...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wouldn't those just be Oceanid Mimics!?

talks.objective: Go to the vantage spot with Arapandu

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! What's over there!? It's magnificent!

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Now Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon know. That is the Varunastra. But the Varuna Contraption is in a deeper place, somewhere as deep as roots.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've underestimated Nara Varuna. Paimon didn't think it would be this big...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Such power is not to be underestimated...

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Before the black rain and before Nara Varuna came to Vana, Aramuhukunda and the Lord of Dendro created the Varuna Contraption. Rain gave life to many things.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Black rain, black mud, and many other bad things made a mess of Vana.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Before {F#he}{M#she} came, Arapandu had never seen such a brave Nara. {F#He}{M#She} fixed the machine together with Aranara, just like the sun driving away the sleepy fog.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Nara Varuna is no longer in Vanarana. Aramuhukunda is no longer in Vanarana... But Aranara must fix the Varuna Contraption again for Festival Utsava and Vana.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We promised Araja and Arama to help prepare for Festival Utsava. As they say, the fire is bigger and stronger when more Nara help pick firewood, right?

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Eek!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um! No, no, Paimon meant that everything will go smoothly with more Nara helping out! Don't be afraid, it has nothing to do with fire! They're not related at all!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, you've outsmarted yourself yet again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, come on. We're here in Sumeru, you know? Paimon just wanted to show everyone that she knows lots of stuff too...

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Arapandu not scared. Paimon has good heart, just like Nara {NICKNAME} and Nara Varuna. Paimon is friend of Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Aranakula, Arabalika, Arakunti, and Arapandu want to heal the Varuna Contraption, but...

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: There are too many spores and Fungi, so we can't do anything.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Arapandu doesn't have a powerful Ararakalari like Arabalika, and the strange rain made the Fungi fiercer...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on. Ararakalari? Arana told Paimon that it can be used to repel Marana...

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Powerful Ararakalari can drive away Fungi. Arapandu's Ararakalari is weak. Can't do anything to Fungi.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Ararakalari can be used that way?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ararakalari should be the general name for a certain type of ability...

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} is smarter than Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Different Aranara have different Ararakalari, but all Aranara gain the power to use it from the plants of Vana.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Arabalika's Ararakalari is very powerful, not afraid of large Fungi and large iron Nara.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Large iron Nara?

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Large iron Nara are very big and have two arms and two legs like Nara {NICKNAME}, but only have one eye.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you're talking about Ruin Guards!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pretty clever, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Oh! There are Fungi on the trees over there... Arabalika can defeat them, but Arapandu can't...

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} not afraid of Fungi either. You do not use Ararakalari, but you are very powerful. Destroy them, like strong gust blowing away a leaf! Whoosh!

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #If not dealt with, spores and Fungi will multiply... Nara {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Leave them to us! Nara {NICKNAME} should be able to deal with them in an instant! Right?

talks.objective: Defeat the Fungi in the trees
Defeat the Fungi in the trees

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the "rest stop," huh? There are some signs that Aranara were here earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Varuna Contraption looks even more impressive from here. Urgh... the pressure is so intense...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, watch out in case you get sucked in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That won't happen! Paimon hopes...?

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: We made an agreement. Will meet up at the "rest stop" after healing the Varuna Contraption's branches and leaves.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Then, we will banish the bad bugs gnawing on the Varuna Contraption's roots and heal it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, what do you mean by "the Varuna Contraption's branches and leaves"?

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: The Varuna Contraption's branches and leaves are everywhere in Vana. They give the machine power to turn black rain into good rain. Good rain then gives things life.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Like how rainwater flows into a stream and then into a lake, the branches and leaves gather bits and pieces that go into the Varuna Contraption.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: The Varuna Contraption is now no longer the same. It is like broken branches have blocked the rainwater, so streams can't form. Without streams, the lake dries out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Urgh... Paimon still doesn't get it...

choices.text: It's basically what happens when you starve.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Paimon won't have strength to work if she doesn't eat! Does this mean the Varuna Contraption is hungry-angry?

choices.text: No, I don't think that's the case...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmm, that's true! No one has the strength to throw a tantrum when they're hungry, anyway!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, we need to heal the branches and leaves first, right?

response.speaker: Arapandu
response.text: #Yes, Arapandu will take Paimon and Nara {NICKNAME} there.

choices.text: It's like when a safe transportation route is blocked by roadblocks...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then we need to clear all the roadblocks to keep going!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We just need to find another path, then! Who decided that we have to take this route anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Paimon never thought that we'd find them in a place like this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on... Eh? You sure these are "branches and leaves"? They look like...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Like stones placed by Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Stone leaves, stone branches. They were created by Aramuhukunda and the Lord of Dendro and can channel Vanarana's power into the Varuna Contraption.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So the Varuna Contraption is like a big tree.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's how it is, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Hmm... Oh no. The three leaves need to be turned to face the branch, but Arapandu is not strong enough.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, you Aranara are kinda small. Don't worry, just leave this to Nara {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Arabalika might be able to do it, but Aranakula and Arakunti...

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Still, we need to solve this problem first. Nara {NICKNAME}, Arapandu will leave it to you.

talks.objective: Make the three "leaves" turn towards the "branch"

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Just turn all three leaves to face the branch. Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}. Leave the rest to Arapandu.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: But it has been too long. Don't know if it will work this time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? There's a chance it can fail?

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: It worked before, but this time it may or may not work. Just like how the sun rose last time and the time before that, but nobody knows if it will rise the next time.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Only after the sun rises next time can Paimon say: "Oh, the sun has risen again."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, wait, that's not good! What if the sun never rises again?

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Paimon, there's no need to be afraid. Nara {NICKNAME} is golden like the sun, just like Nara Varuna. A brave Nara, Nara {NICKNAME} is.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Nara Varuna returned the moon and sun to us. Nara {NICKNAME} can also do that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...Yes! Paimon also believes in {NICKNAME}. {F#She}{M#He} can overcome any difficulty!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't you worry.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: But for now, leave this to Arapandu.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon thinks it... worked?

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Yes, the branch and leaves here are healed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's great! And your Aranara dance was really interesting, too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You could learn some fancy footwork from the Aranara, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like a great idea!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I mean, more exercise will be good for you, given how much you eat...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey! Paimon's been running around everywhere with you, {NICKNAME}. That counts as exercise!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, this won't be enough to fix the Varuna Contraption, will it?

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: There are three more places like this in Vana. Arabalika is very strong and might succeed... But Arapandu's very worried about Aranakula and Arakunti. Vana has become more dangerous after the strange rain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What say we help you go check on them, then? After all, we can't prepare for Festival Utsava in peace if the Varuna Contraption isn't fixed.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #With the help of Paimon and Nara {NICKNAME}, the Varuna Contraption will surely be fixed soon. Life will return to Vana like before.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Aranakula went to the <color=#00E1FFFF>Yasna Monument</color>. There is an Aranara memorial to Nara Varuna in the depths of Vana, but we haven't been there for a long time because of the Fungi and spores.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Aranakula is used to being with soil and seeds. Familiar with all things born from the soil.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Find him. Tell him Arapandu's name. Then he will not be afraid.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? He sounds like a rather timid Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Arabalika's Ararakalari is very strong! But... But please, Paimon and Nara {NICKNAME}, go check on him...

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Arabalika is at the <color=#00E1FFFF>Ruins of Dahri</color>. That place smells like iron so much... Paimon and Nara {NICKNAME} must be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We will, thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Arakunti is at the <color=#00E1FFFF>Grove of Dreams</color>. You can enter dreams from there. He and Nara have a... distant relationship. If he hides, play our music.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of that, didn't we get an Aranara music score earlier? We can try playing that if we can't find Arakunti.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Arapandu will wait at the "rest stop" and observe how Vana is doing.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: Aranakula, Arabalika, and Arakunti know to meet up at the "rest stop" after healing the branches and leaves.

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: #Golden Nara, brave Nara. May Aramuhukunda watch over Nara {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup! You can count on us!
